question.text: What is the fundamental role of a 'scheduled offence' in the context of money laundering under PMLA?

answer.text: It serves as the predicate offence that generates proceeds of crime, which is a prerequisite for the offence of money laundering to arise
It refers to any minor offence that is scheduled for hearing in a court of law
It is an offence committed by government officials as per a pre-planned schedule
It is an offence that has been de-criminalized and no longer carries any penalty

explanation.text: The Logic: A scheduled offence must have been committed and proceeds of crime generated before the offence of money laundering can arise under PMLA. Scheduled offences therefore form the foundation for money laundering because they are the predicate offences that produce the proceeds of crime. The Trap: Option B uses the word 'scheduled' in its everyday court-hearing sense; in PMLA, 'scheduled' means offences listed in the Schedule to the Act. Note: Without an underlying scheduled offence that generates proceeds of crime, the PMLA money-laundering charge cannot be sustained.
